title: Android Safe Mode: How to Turn It On and Off, and What It Tells You
html:
Safe mode starts the phone with only its built-in apps, so you can tell whether a downloaded app is behind a problem. If the problem goes away in Safe mode, an app you installed is likely the cause. Remove recently installed apps one at a time, restarting normally after each, until the problem stops.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026. The key combination depends on the brand and the model.

I checked the Safe mode option on a vivo V23 Pro running Android 14 (Funtouch OS 14) on 10 Oct 2026. I got as far as the Safe mode prompt and tapped Cancel, so I did not restart into Safe mode on this phone. The Pixel and Samsung steps below come from Google and Samsung and I did not try them myself.

What Safe mode does

Google's help says safe mode removes some Home screen widgets and is a way to check whether downloaded apps are causing a problem. Samsung describes it as running the basic operating system with most third-party apps disabled.

Pixel

  • Pixel 6 and later, to turn on: press and hold the Power and Volume up buttons for a few seconds, then touch and hold Power off or Restart, and tap OK.
  • Pixel 5a and earlier, to turn on: press and hold Power, tap Power off. When the animation starts, press and hold Volume down until the animation ends and the phone starts in safe mode.
  • To turn off, Pixel 6 and later: press and hold Power and Volume up for a few seconds, then tap Restart. On Pixel 5a and earlier, press and hold Power for about 30 seconds, or until it restarts.

Samsung Galaxy

  • To turn on, method 1: press the Volume down and Power keys together (or tap the Power icon in the quick panel), press and hold Power off, then tap Safe mode.
  • To turn on, method 2: switch the phone on, and when the Samsung logo appears hold the Volume down key.
  • To turn off: restart the phone, or tap the Safe mode notification and tap Turn off. The phone restarts.

Samsung notes that screens and settings vary by model and software version, and that the side key should be set to open the Power off menu for the first method.

Other brands

The steps differ for Xiaomi, Redmi, realme, Oppo, Vivo, OnePlus, Motorola and others. Check your maker's support page for your model.

On my vivo V23 Pro (Funtouch OS 14), pressing and holding Power off in the power menu opens a box titled "Reboot to safe mode". It says: "Do you want to reboot into safe mode? This will disable all third party applications you have installed. They will be restored when you reboot again." The buttons are Cancel and OK. I tapped Cancel, so I have not seen the restart itself or the way back out on this phone.

Use Safe mode to find the problem app

  1. Start the phone in Safe mode and use it normally. Does the problem go away?
  2. If it does, leave Safe mode and remove the apps you installed recently, one at a time. Restart normally after each.
  3. When the problem stops, the last app you removed was the cause. You can install the others again.

If the problem does not go away in Safe mode, the cause is not a downloaded app. Look at slowness fixes or battery drain, or see a service centre. If you suspect harmful software, see our phone check.

What to do next

  1. Start in Safe mode and test the problem.
  2. Remove recent apps one at a time, restarting normally each time.
  3. If nothing changes, the app is not the cause.

Sources

  • Find problem apps by rebooting to safe mode on Android (Android Help)
